name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine
tagline: Digital archive of the World Wide Web — preserving over 1 trillion web pages since 1996
dependency_risks: Legal copyright battles threatening operational scope

news_articles.headline: Internet Archive suffers data breach exposing 31 million user accounts
Publishers win copyright lawsuit against Internet Archive over digital lending

academic_citations: Kahle, B. (2007). 'Preserving the Internet.' Scientific American, 296(3), 40-47.
Bragg, M. (2012). 'Building the Internet Archive.' In The Internet Archive: A Digital Library of Internet Sites and Other Cultural Artifacts.
Dougherty, J. & Meyer, D. (2014). 'Migrating Complex Projects to an Open-Source Platform: The Internet Archive Experience.' Code4Lib Journal, 24.
Multiple citations in legal proceedings (Hachette v. Internet Archive, 2020-2023)
awards: National Medal of Technology and Innovation (Brewster Kahle, 2015)
Recognition as UNESCO Memory of the World candidate

policy_outcomes.description: Google announced collaboration to surface Wayback Machine links in search results for unavailable pages

outcome_methodology: Institutional adoption; legal proceedings reference archive as authoritative source; journalists and researchers routinely cite captures
documented_limitations: Robots.txt exclusions allow sites to opt out of archiving
Not all web content is preserved (dark web, paywalled, dynamic content)
failure_modes: Centralised data risk despite Canadian mirror plans
governance_model: nonprofit governed by Brewster Kahle as founder; board of directors
curation_criteria: Automated web crawl; respects robots.txt; supplemented by voluntary uploads and partner digitisation projects
contributor_governance: Open submissions; partner institutions; staff-managed archive decisions
controversies: Hachette v. Internet Archive (2020-2023): publishers sued over controlled digital lending; court ruled against Archive
Music industry lawsuit (2023) over Great 78 Project; settled September 2025
October 2024 data breach: 31 million user accounts compromised; SN_BLACKMETA hacker group claimed responsibility
legal_regulatory_issues: Major copyright litigation: Hachette v. Internet Archive (lost 2023); music industry suit (settled 2025); data breach October 2024
government_partnerships: Library of Congress (collaboration on digital preservation)
ai_involvement: Machine learning used for optical character recognition (OCR) on digitized texts; AI-assisted metadata generation; no AI involvement in civic/electoral processes
